_comment: The three operator income models. Derived from knowledge/02-income-models.md (last_verified 2026-07-11) and lib/offers.ts. Ranges are honest and hedged on purpose — no invented stats, no income promises.

models.name: Services — sell agent-assisted delivery
models.summary: Sell an outcome to a specific client; your agent team compresses delivery cost while you keep discovery, trust, and the final gate. The funding stage, not the destination.
models.timeToFirstDollar: typically days to weeks — depends entirely on your existing network and ability to scope real work
models.upfrontCost: near zero beyond an agent runtime subscription; the real investment is scoping and trust-building time
models.laborProfile: labor-coupled: your hours cap revenue. Agents compress delivery, not discovery or client trust. Cap concurrent clients before quality collapses.
models.failureMode: scope creep — agents make delivery cheap but discovery expensive — and staying here forever instead of skimming service weeks into building products

models.name: Products — sell what your agents help you build
models.summary: Package the decisions you made in service work — templates, packs, kits, agent-native products — and sell them self-serve through a merchant of record.
models.timeToFirstDollar: typically weeks to months — volume is the whole game, and volume comes from distribution you already have or must build
models.upfrontCost: low cash, high time: a merchant of record takes a per-sale fee instead of upfront cost, but the build and the audience are unpaid until they compound
models.laborProfile: front-loaded build plus a permanent maintenance promise — a product is a promise of upkeep, and stale products refund
models.failureMode: no distribution — the product is rarely the bottleneck, the audience is

models.name: Systems — operate assets with maintenance measured honestly
models.summary: Own an asset that produces income with maintenance measured in hours per month — a publication, an evergreen product line, a disclosed affiliate property.
models.timeToFirstDollar: typically weeks to months — the slowest of the three; the compounding asset is usually distribution, not the content itself
models.upfrontCost: hosting and tooling are cheap; the real cost is months of unpaid compounding time before the asset carries itself
models.laborProfile: structurally decoupled from hours, never zero — every real system has a maintenance floor, and we publish it instead of pretending otherwise
models.failureMode: pretending 'passive' means zero hours, then abandoning the maintenance floor until the asset decays
